messages:
maya: Noticed a weird spike in SAST alerts during the nightly pipeline after the RBAC rename + KMS rotation. Several findings flagged in infra/dast/runner.go that look like leaked header handling. Opening thread to coordinate triage.

tom-scanner: Saw that too. Our DAST runner started failing auth checks and then printed debug headers to stdout for a couple of retries. Happened around 2026-03-03T03:14:10Z. I think the token provider returned an error and the code fell back to logging the raw header for troubleshooting.

build-bot: CI pipeline 2026-03-03-03:09: run-1245: sast-scan FAILED (new findings: 4). Link: https://ci.example/runs/1245

rachel-infra: Context: we renamed RBAC principal svc/dast-runner -> svc/dast-scan at 2026-03-02T23:50Z and rotated staging KMS key at 2026-03-02T22:00Z. Both changes were low-risk but may have combined to break secret fetch logic.

maya: Can we get the exact file/line flagged by SAST? If it's printing headers we need to patch fast and treat it as potential PII/secret exposure.

tom-scanner: SAST points to infra/dast/runner.go: lines 278-291 where we call getToken(); on error we log the request with debug: log.Debugf("request: %s", req.Headers). I'll open a PR to stop logging headers and to redact Authorization headers in the logger.

kevin-sre: Immediate containment suggestions: (1) revoke staging token(s) that the runner uses, (2) disable auto-retries in scanner to avoid repeated leaked logs, (3) add a temporary filter on the logging pipeline to drop Authorization header values from stored logs.

sec-oncall: Agreed. Also create an evidence bundle before we redact anything so compliance/audit can see the original as-of-time artifact. We'll store the bundle in secure bucket and attach HMAC manifest.

maya: Proposed quick-fix (PR text):
```
- log.Debugf("request: %s", req.Headers)
+ // redact Authorization header before logging
+ if req.Headers.Get("Authorization") != "" {
+   req.Headers.Set("Authorization", "[REDACTED]")
+ }
+ log.Debugf("request: %s", req.Headers)
```
I'll add a unit test that simulates a request and asserts logs do not contain "Bearer".

rachel-infra: On audit mapping: because of the RBAC rename, Cloud audit entries show both principals. I'll run a mapping job that rewrites older principal names to canonical form and produce a CSV with fields: timestamp, original_principal, canonical_principal, resource, action, log_id. Example command I'll run: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="svc/dast-*"' --start=2026-03-02T22:00:00Z --end=2026-03-03T04:00:00Z --format json > dast-principals.json`

kevin-sre: For evidence preservation, run: `tar czf evidence-3470004322.tar.gz --files-from evidence-list.txt && aws s3 cp evidence-3470004322.tar.gz s3://redwood-sec/incidents/INC-2026-045/` then `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$HMAC_KEY" -binary evidence-3470004322.tar.gz | base64 > evidence-3470004322.sha256` attach both to JIRA.

tom-scanner: I've opened PR: https://git.example/infra/dast/pull/102 to remove header logging and to default the scanner config `auth.enabled` to `false` for staging clusters. Also disabled auto-retry.

maya: I'll start the SAST re-run after PR merges. If the static checker flags similar patterns elsewhere (e.g., other clients), mark as high priority.

sec-oncall: Logged incident INC-2026-045. Owners: infra-oncall, sec-audit. Please add timeline notes to the ticket.

kevin-sre: Quick logging pipeline mitigation: add a Fluentd filter to mask Authorization header before writing to backend. Example sed we can use in a filter: `sed -E 's/(Authorization:\s*)Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/\1[REDACTED]/g'` — I'll coordinate with logging team.

rachel-infra: One more: we should add a pre-scan CI gate that ensures `auth.enabled` is either false for staging or that the referenced secretRef resolves in vault. Pseudocode for the hook: `if env==staging && auth.enabled==true && !vault.exists(secretRef) -> fail`. I'll draft a GitHub Actions job.

maya: Also adding a SAST rule suppression policy: if a finding is a true-positive (saw token in logs), it must be remediated and re-run; otherwise follow FP workflow in docs. Link to suppression policy: https://wiki.example/sec/sast-suppression

tom-scanner: Running the log scan for 2026-03-02T22:00Z..2026-03-03T04:00Z now and will post container IDs and any outbound IPs we see. If we find egress to unexpected hosts, we'll escalate to sec immediately.

sec-oncall: Schedule a 90-min postmortem tomorrow 10:00-11:30; please attach evidence and remediation PRs to the incident. No public disclosure required.

maya: Thanks. After this we should add a detection rule: alert on any logging that matches regex `Authorization:\s*Bearer` across prod/staging indices. Prefer an oncall pager for prod matches and a slack alert for staging.

kevin-sre: Will open follow-up tickets: LOG-123 (masking pipeline), SAST-456 (rule hardening), CI-789 (pre-scan hook).

rachel-infra: Uploaded evidence bundle to s3://redwood-sec/incidents/INC-2026-045/evidence-3470004322.tar.gz and posted signed manifest to the ticket.

tom-scanner: All done on my side: PR merged, staging canary rolled, scanner creds revoked. Will monitor logs for any residual findings.

maya: Re-run SAST passed on the hotfix branch. Closing this thread unless new findings appear. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
